story:
Caldey was Avalon's burying isle. The colleges sent their dead across the water to it for longer than they kept count, and the priests of the dead who lived there planted rowans round the graves to keep them lying down. The graveyard on the western strand, nearest the door of Arawn's gaol, was the one the priests feared most, because a grave beside a door is a grave that someone may try to open from the other side. So they set a sexton over it who did not sleep at night, and walked the rows with a lantern, and cut the rowans back when they grew so thick they hid the stones.

The fishermen of Little Haven remember him only as the sexton. He had a name; it is on a stone in that graveyard, they say, which he cut himself and left blank at the bottom for the year. He kept the strand graves through the plague years and the long quiet, and on the night the colleges burned he was still there, walking the rows, when the boats came over from Avalon with the last of the college dead. He buried them. The last he buried was a girl of the colleges, a young sorceress called Eralyne, who had come over on the boats alive and died on the strand before morning.

Then the witch called, and the isle stood up, and the sexton stood up with it. He keeps the graveyard still. He walks the rows with no lantern and the rowans have grown wild, and what he keeps in is no longer the same as what he kept out. The fishermen say he is the only one of Caldey's dead who still does the work he did alive, and that he does it the wrong way round now: he keeps the living away from the graves, and the dead in them up. He stands over Eralyne most of all, because she was the last one he put down, and the first he failed to keep there.

He does not sleep, the fishermen say, and the crypt's dead are his, and Eralyne is his; trouble him with more than a pair of hands and she comes up the row to him. When he is put down he is at his rows again before the gulls settle. Ariette of Fort Gwyntell, who wants the girl's soul set free, says the sexton is the harder half of the work, and the sadder.
legend: The Crypt Guardian is a level 59 undead at the graveyard by the Caer Sidi strand on Caldey's west coast, with Eralyne (55) about 600 away. Both are Undead Servants of Morgana and aggressive from about 500. A pair can usually pull the guardian alone; a bigger group widens the bring-a-friend call to 600 and up, and then Eralyne walks over to join, so either keep the pull small or plan to fight both. An ancient zombie stands about 430 off. No spells or styles in the data: a straight melee fight with a 59, a full group of fifties. Lost Treasure (Ariette) needs Eralyne; the guardian is in the way. Respawn about 80 seconds.

loremasterTopic.text: The sexton of the graveyard nearest Caer Sidi's door on [caldey], who kept the strand graves against whatever might open them from the other side. He buried the last of the college dead on the night of the burning, [eralyne] last of all, and stood up with the isle when the witch called. He keeps the rows still, the wrong way round: the living out, the dead up.

bookPage: From the Ledger of Little Haven, kept by Mordwywr, enchanter. Paid to nobody, but entered: the fishermen tell me there is a stone in the strand graveyard with the sexton's own name cut on it by his own hand, and the year left blank. I went to see. I found the stone. The name is worn and I could not read it; the bottom of the stone is blank and clean, as though someone keeps it so. The sexton was three rows off, standing over the girl's grave. He did not come for me. I think he was busy. I have entered the stone in the ledger as unpaid, because I do not know who owes what to whom.
